question: Which of the following varnas in Vedic society was considered responsible for trade and business?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Vaishya**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In the **Vedic society**, the social structure was divided into four **varnas (classes)**, namely Brahmin, Kshatriya, Vaishya, and Shudra, each with specific duties and responsibilities.
 
• The **Vaishya varna** was primarily responsible for trade, commerce, and agricultural activities. They played a significant role in the economic development of society.
 
• Vaishyas were engaged in professions like **merchants, traders, artisans, and agriculturalists**, contributing significantly to the prosperity and wealth of the community.
 
• They were regarded as the backbone of the economy, focusing on **wealth generation and distribution** through their business and agricultural practices.
 
• Unlike Brahmins (scholars and priests) and Kshatriyas (warriors and rulers), the Vaishyas held a crucial position in ensuring the smooth functioning of the **economic and trade systems** of the Vedic age.
